elements.requirement: The Mental Capacity Act 2005 does not authorise any person (“D”) to deprive any other person (“P”) of his liberty.
elements.quote: This Act does not authorise any person (“D”) to deprive any other person (“P”) of his liberty

elements.requirement: The general lack of authority under the Mental Capacity Act 2005 for a person (“D”) to deprive another person (“P”) of liberty is subject to the provisions of section 4A and section 4B.
elements.quote: subject to— (a) the following provisions of this section, and (b) section 4B

elements.requirement: A person (“D”) may deprive another person (“P”) of his liberty if, by doing so, D is giving effect to a relevant decision of the court.
elements.quote: D may deprive P of his liberty if, by doing so, D is giving effect to a relevant decision of the court

elements.requirement: A relevant decision of the court is defined as a decision made by an order under section 16(2)(a) in relation to a matter concerning the personal welfare of the person (“P”).
elements.quote: A relevant decision of the court is a decision made by an order under section 16(2)(a) in relation to a matter concerning P's personal welfare

elements.requirement: A person (“D”) may deprive another person (“P”) of his liberty if the deprivation is authorised by Schedule A1 concerning hospital and care home residents.
elements.quote: D may deprive P of his liberty if the deprivation is authorised by Schedule A1 (hospital and care home residents: deprivation of liberty)
